title: Theo and the Confession
premise: Kestrel Pemberton, a discreet estate lawyer known for handling the wills of the wealthy and the dead, is hired by an elderly client who pays in advance to prove that his own murder has not yet happened — only that it is scheduled. Following a trail of forged death certificates, Kestrel finds a ledger hidden in plain sight among his firm's own archives, recording decades of bribes, inheritances, and quietly arranged deaths tied to the powerful Ashcombe family. As the anniversary dinner approaches — the date when the next 'death' is penciled in — Kestrel must choose between protecting his client, exposing the network, and preserving his own carefully invisible life. In the end, he leaks the ledger on the night of the dinner, letting justice arrive outside the courtroom, though it costs him his practice, his anonymity, and nearly his life.
about_author: Tamsin Sandoval spent eleven years as a probate clerk in a coastal English town before turning to fiction, drawing on the quiet dramas of wills, estates, and family secrets. She writes mysteries about ordinary professionals dragged into extraordinary moral corners.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Kestrel Pemberton's POV. A frail new client, Edmund Voss, retains Kestrel with an unusual request: prove that his murder — planned but not yet committed — can be prevented, and pay him triple upfront. The emotional beat is unease; Kestrel's instinct to stay invisible wars with curiosity.

chapters.title: A Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. While verifying Voss's assets, Kestrel discovers a sealed will dated three years in the future, naming beneficiaries who are all still alive. He realizes someone inside the legal system drafted it. Beat: cold dread beneath professional composure.

chapters.title: The Ashcombe Name
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The future will ties into the Ashcombe estate, whose patriarch died a year ago under circumstances ruled natural. Kestrel interviews the widow, Vivian Ashcombe, at their crumbling manor. Beat: seductive menace; she knows more than she says.

chapters.title: Death Certificates in Duplicate
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Cross-checking records, Kestrel finds four Ashcombe-adjacent deaths with duplicate certificates — one filed, one altered. Someone with registry access has been rewriting endings. Beat: the thrill of the hunt shadowed by fear of being noticed.

chapters.title: The Partner's Warning
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. His law partner, Marguerite Hale, warns him off the case, revealing she once refused Ashcombe money years ago. First hint of the firm's complicity. Beat: loyalty strained; Kestrel wonders what else she's hiding.

chapters.title: Voss Disappears
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. When he returns with questions, Voss's flat is emptied and the old man gone, leaving only a hotel key and a note: 'The ledger remembers.' Beat: abandonment and resolve; Kestrel is now committed whether he likes it or not.

chapters.title: What the Registry Clerk Saw
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Nell Okafor, a junior registry clerk who noticed the duplicate certificates and was paid to forget. She tells Kestrel about a man with a lawyer's briefcase who visited monthly. Beat: solidarity between small people against large machinery.

chapters.title: Dinner Invitations
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. An invitation arrives to the Ashcombe anniversary dinner — addressed to him by name, though he never revealed his involvement. The message is clear: he is being watched. Beat: paranoia tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Confession
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She admits the firm laundered Ashcombe bequests for thirty years under her predecessor, and that the 'future will' was drafted by her late mentor. Beat: guilt finally spoken aloud; trust rebuilt, then immediately tested.

chapters.title: The Ledger Hidden in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Decoding Voss's note, Kestrel finds the ledger bound as a dummy probate volume in the firm's own archive — initials, dates, payments, and a column of scheduled deaths. The anniversary dinner date appears beside Voss's name. Beat: horrified clarity.

chapters.title: Nineteen Names
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Marguerite's shared investigation, alternating close-third. Nineteen names in the ledger match unsolved or 'natural' deaths across two decades. Beat: grief accumulating; each name was someone's whole world.

chapters.title: Vivian's Version
chapters.summary: Vivian Ashcombe's POV. She reveals her husband discovered the ledger and died within a month; she has played the grieving widow while gathering evidence of her own. Beat: ambiguous alliance — is she ally, architect, or both?

chapters.title: The Man with the Briefcase
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel identifies the registry visitor as Corwin Ashe, the family solicitor and the network's operational hand. A near-miss tail through the city leaves Kestrel shaken. Beat: pursuit; the hunter glimpses being hunted.

chapters.title: A Price on Silence
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Ashe offers Kestrel a partnership, a house, and erasure of his debts to walk away — then makes it clear refusal means becoming a name in the ledger. Beat: temptation laid bare; power corrupting by offer rather than force.

chapters.title: Nell Pays the Price
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. After helping Kestrel again, Nell is attacked and her flat ransacked; she survives and goes to ground with Marguerite. Beat: guilt and fury; the cost of truth lands on the innocent first.

chapters.title: Forging the Counterfeit Will
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Marguerite's POV. To buy time, they draft a decoy version of the future will with poisoned provisions, hoping to flush out whoever expects to collect. Beat: cunning rising; lawyers fighting with their own weapons.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Anniversary
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Voss resurfaces, half-broken, hiding in a chapel; he confirms the dinner is the trigger date and gives Kestrel the final cipher key. Beat: fragile hope; two frightened men choosing courage over safety.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, embedded at the Ashcombe table under a borrowed invitation. Toasts rise, Ashe watches him, and Vivian plays her double game to the hilt. Beat: exquisite tension; every glass raised is a threat disguised as celebration.

chapters.title: Exposure
chapters.summary: Climax, Kestrel's POV. During the toast, Kestrel triggers the leak — the full ledger goes to press, police, and every named beneficiary simultaneously. Ashe moves to silence him; Vivian turns on Ashe with her own recorded evidence. Beat: chaos breaking open; truth detonating mid-toast.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Ashe flees and dies fleeing — officially an accident, and Kestrel chooses not to contest the story, understanding some justice must live outside courtrooms. Vivian claims the estate to dismantle the network from within. Beat: bitter triumph; victory with blood on its hands.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Visible Man
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The scandal ends his firm; Marguerite retires, Nell testifies safely, and Voss lives out his days un-murdered. Kestrel, once invisible, is now a public name. Beat: loss and liberation entwined; he mourns the self he had to spend.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair at Dinner
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Kestrel's POV. One year later, Kestrel hosts a modest dinner for the survivors of the nineteen names. He raises a glass to those who couldn't come, keeping the ledger's last blank page as a promise. Beat: quiet resolution; memory as the truest estate.
